verdict_reason: The errors map shape is correct and matches the handler, but the record's camelCase wire names contradict the in-repo locked contract and no required-mode annotations make errors optional in the published spec.

todos.issue: errors map SHAPE (Map<field,List<message>>) matches the handler and the contract, but the CASING contradicts the in-repo docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml added by this same PR: the locked ValidationProblem says keys are 'ALWAYS the wire names (address_line_1, never addressLine1)' and Problem declares trace_id, while this record declares traceId and its Javadoc mandates camelCase keys; camelCase is not in the contract's 'Declared deviations' list and OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate compares only path sets, HTTP methods, operationIds and the 400 anyOf, so the schema-level drift ships silently
todos.fix: Re-copy the locked contract with camelCase Problem/ValidationProblem schemas, examples and prose (traceId, errors keyed addressLine1) recorded as a cv-001 deviation — the code, ITs and ins-frontend (errors.addressLine1) are all camelCase — and extend the divergence gate to compare schema property names so this cannot drift again

todos.issue: No @Schema(requiredMode = REQUIRED) on any component, so springdoc emits ValidationProblem (and Problem) with no required list at all — see the committed docs/openapi/operators.yml ValidationProblem schema, which has properties but no 'required'. The locked contract declares ValidationProblem as allOf [Problem, {required: [errors]}] with Problem requiring type/title/status; the published spec therefore makes 'errors' — the one field that distinguishes the validation-error branch from the bad-request branch — optional, and generated clients get a nullable map on the commonest 400
todos.fix: Annotate the record components with @Schema(requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED) on type, title, status and errors (leave detail/traceId optional) and regenerate docs/openapi/operators.yml with -Dopenapi.generate=true
